## 5dbe4bcb101c

**Classification: reproduced teaching defect and contract failures.** Generator SHA-256 `6633f6dbac5d4824f5cbd97720f1ae1259dfead614130e725beb7241ef87ce28`; selected rule hash `78316577904e`.

The four targeted shared gates all failed: lint lacks `RULE_HASH` and has dead axes; defect lint reports dead/overlapping textures plus validator impostors; the override gate reports more than 13,650 findings and 65,070 undeclared multi-axis rejections; semantic gate fails because no contract is declared. Retained command results are under `checks/audit/5dbe4bcb101c-{lint,defect_lint,override,semantic_gate}/`.

A custom 1,000-draw-per-band probe found that easy emits exactly one marker candidate in **1,000/1,000** draws, so it cannot teach which candidate should be selected. Medium has multiple candidates in 493/1,000 draws and hard in 1,000/1,000, but complete lessons can still be ambiguous.

Concrete default-domain counterexample: medium, `seed=0`, four demonstrations starting at `sample_index=5`. The plausible rival “extract the largest marker-colored blob” matches all four demonstrations but differs on the next generated query. The selected Racket rule returns `[[7],[7]]`; the rival returns `[[7,7,7]]`. Exact grid, schedule and outputs are in `checks/audit/5dbe4bcb101c-probe.json`; the supported Racket replay with source/rule/input hashes is `checks/audit/5dbe4bcb101c-query-racket.json` (input `checks/audit/5dbe4bcb101c-query-input.json`). This is a generated default input, not a hand-written out-of-domain adversary.

The override probe also shows accepted byte-identical controls for `n_marker_blobs` and `shape_size`, plus an accepted unknown key. `marker_color=9` was byte-identical in the chosen seed because 9 was also the default observed marker, so that single observation is not by itself evidence that the axis is dead.

## 5dbe4bcb101c

**Finding: the current four-demonstration sampler still admits the largest-blob shortcut; several advertised controls remain ineffective.** This independently reproduces an unresolved finding already attached to the same current source, rather than claiming a new defect on different bytes.

Audited generator SHA-256: `6633f6dbac5d4824f5cbd97720f1ae1259dfead614130e725beb7241ef87ce28` (v2.1.0). Selected/executed canonical rule hash: `78316577904e`. The rule reads the first nonzero top-row marker, finds same-color 4-connected components of size greater than one, and crops the topmost candidate, breaking row ties by leftmost column.

**Exact generated witness:** medium difficulty, `seed=0`, four demonstrations at sample indices **5–8**, followed by query **9**. A separately implemented rival that instead crops the **largest** eligible marker-color component agrees with all four demonstrations but changes the query. Every input passes the current validator (`[]`). The official Racket rule returns **`[[7],[7]]`**, while the rival returns **`[[7,7,7]]`**. Racket replay verified all five generated lesson labels and all three public canonical labels, with matching source/rule hashes. The three canonical examples each have one eligible component and therefore also fit this rival. The generator declares `EXAMPLES_NEEDED = 4` but has no executable lesson guard to reject this ambiguity.

A fresh 100-draw-per-band census (`seed=1000+i`, `sample_index=i`, `i=0..99`) found one eligible candidate in **100/100 easy**, one/two candidates in **48/52 medium**, and two/three candidates in **48/52 hard** draws. Thus the easy distribution does not demonstrate a choice between eligible candidates. These census counts use the independent parser; the eight explicit witness/canonical inputs were checked through Racket.

**Additional exact control witnesses:** at medium `seed=0`, `sample_index=0`, `marker_color=2` is accepted but produces marker color **7** and a byte-identical grid to the default. The declared `n_marker_blobs=3` and `shape_size=7` controls also return that same grid, whose eligible components have sizes **3 and 4**. An unknown key is accepted unchanged. These are fresh checks of four named controls, not a rerun of the historical exhaustive override gate.

Evidence is self-contained under `checks/audit/5dbe4bcb101c/`: `probe.py` contains the independent parser/rival; `report.json` retains the full lesson, source/rule identities, seeds, validator results, actual/rival outputs, canonical observations, census and controls; `query_witness.json` is the single-query witness; `input.json` and `racket.json` retain the supported authority replay; `command-records.json` records exact working directories, argv, exit status and logs. The preparation, official apply, and verification commands all exited **0**. The final verifier checked the actual Racket inputs/outputs and unchanged audited source hash.

**Scope:** findings-only review of current source, public canonical examples, current notes and review index; no task-local tests exist. No broad battery was rerun. The audited generator, notes, evidence index, catalog and shared tools were left unchanged, including the existing `needs_triage` audit status. This review supplies reproducible evidence for repair and does not approve or patch the audited task.
